draft.title: What competitive advantage is
card: Rivals are businesses that sell similar goods or services to the same customers. Customers choose between them.
A competitive advantage is something a business has that makes customers choose it over its rivals.
It can be something customers see, such as a lower price or better quality. It can also be something behind the scenes, such as cheaper ways of making the product.
A business with a competitive advantage can win more sales, and that can help it earn more profit.
draft.remember: A competitive advantage is the reason customers pick one business and not its rivals.

a.q: What is the best description of a competitive advantage?
opts: Something that makes customers choose a business over rivals
Something that makes a business larger than all its rivals
Something that lets a business charge any price it likes
Something that a business has but its rivals do not want
a.why: A competitive advantage is about winning customers from rivals. Being larger is not the same thing: a big business can still lose customers to a smaller one that offers something they prefer.
a.clue: Think about what customers do when they have a choice.

b.q: Two bakeries sit on the same street in Geelong and sell similar bread. Priya's bakery is bigger, but most locals buy from Tom's, because his bread is fresher. What does this show?
opts: Tom's freshness is a competitive advantage
Priya's size is a competitive advantage
Neither bakery has a competitive advantage
Both bakeries share the same competitive advantage
b.why: Customers choose Tom's over a rival because of fresher bread, so freshness is his competitive advantage. Size alone is not an advantage here, because it does not make customers choose Priya's.
b.clue: Look for what is making customers choose.

a.best: Something that makes customers choose a business over rivals

b.best: Tom's freshness is a competitive advantage
